title: Asynchronous Feedback Framework for Distributed Teams
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary:
This page documents Redwood's recommended asynchronous feedback framework designed for distributed teams (multiple time zones, flexible schedules, and hybrid work). It defines principles, step-by-step processes, manager responsibilities, message templates, tooling integrations, and metrics for measuring effectiveness. The goal is to preserve feedback cadence and quality while respecting heads-down time and global schedules.

Why this exists:
- Synchronous 1:1s and review meetings are not always possible across time zones.
- Teams need reliable, documented feedback to support onboarding, performance calibration, and continuous development.
- Asynchronous channels (written feedback, structured forms, and recorded comments) reduce meeting overload and create auditable history for coaching and promotion decisions.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to all teams at Redwood with distributed contributors, including engineering, product, sales engineering, and support.
- Primary focus: feedback that would otherwise be given in a 1:1 or a manager check-in. Not intended to replace formal performance review cycles (those remain calendarized).

Principles (short):
1) Timely: aim to provide feedback within 72 hours for task-level feedback and within 7 days for developmental feedback.
2) Actionable: include specific examples, impact, and next steps.
3) Respectful & private: use direct channels for sensitive topics; public praise is encouraged, private coaching is required.
4) Accessible record: store feedback in the agreed tooling so it is discoverable for mentoring and review.
5) Lightweight & consistent: use templates to reduce cognitive load and surface signal across distributed teams.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Contributor (peer): Provide concise, example-driven feedback when requested or observed. Use the "Task Feedback" template for single tasks and "Developmental Snapshot" for themes.
- Manager: Curate asynchronous inputs, synthesize into coaching notes, follow up in one sync or asynchronous message, and escalate concerns where necessary. Managers own the cadence and ensure no contributor goes without manager-sourced feedback for >30 days.
- People Ops: Maintain templates, run tooling integrations, and measure adoption and quality metrics.

Core artifacts and tooling integrations:
- Feedback repository: Redwood Feedback (internal) / Notion / Google Drive (centralized depending on team); recommended: Redwood Feedback for integrated tagging with performance reviews.
- Slack channels: #team-praise (public), DMs for private coaching. Use Slack thread for short task-level clarifications only.
- Async forms: A lightweight form for "Developmental Snapshot" (name, context, observation, impact, suggested next step). Form saves to the feedback repo.
- Video recording: Use Loom for complex feedback that benefits from tone and walkthroughs. Attach link to the feedback entry.

Process: Asynchronous 1:1 (manager-led cadence)
1) Pre-week (optional): Manager adds a 5-item "checklist" in the feedback tool summarizing themes they plan to address.
2) Mid-week: Peers add any task-level feedback entries (optional).
3) Weekly summary (manager): Prior to the end of the week, manager composes a 5–10 sentence synthesis for each direct report containing:
   - One win (specific)
   - One opportunity (specific)
   - One suggested next action with owner and timeline
4) Delivery: Post the summary in a private feedback entry (tagged) and send a short Slack DM alert: "Your weekly update is posted — please review when you have time."
5) Follow-up: If the contributor does not acknowledge within 5 business days, manager schedules a 20-minute sync or asks for written acknowledgement.

Process: Task-level feedback (peer-to-peer)
1) When a peer notices a signal worth capturing, they open the feedback form and fill: context, what happened, impact, and suggested next step.
2) Keep entries <= 200 words and include links to artifacts (PRs, tickets).
3) Tag the recipient and relevant manager. If the matter is sensitive, send directly to the manager.

Onboarding-specific flows:
- Day 1–30: New hires should receive at least one manager-synthesized async summary per week plus two peer developmental snapshots (mentor/partner).
- Days 31–90: Weekly manager summaries continue but can reduce to every-other-week after 60 days if the new hire and manager agree.
- Buddy system: The onboarding buddy must supply at least three short notes (knowledge handoffs, cultural tips, quick wins) to the feedback repo in the first 30 days.

Templates (copyable):
- Task Feedback (<=200 words):
  Subject: Task feedback — [ticket/PR #]
  Context: (1 line)
  Observation: (what you saw)
  Impact: (why it mattered)
  Suggested next step: (owner & timeline)

- Developmental Snapshot (up to 400 words):
  Context: (project and timeframe)
  Theme: (communication / technical depth / ownership / collaboration)
  Concrete example(s): (links + bullets)
  Effect on team/product: (short)
  Suggested coachable move: (manager or peer action + timeframe)

Example weekly manager synthesis (5–10 sentences):
- Win: "Great job closing the memory-leak bug in PR #452 — your root-cause analysis cut projected customer impact by ~40%."
- Opportunity: "We saw slower cross-team follow-up; consider adding a one-line summary and next-action in tickets to speed handoffs."
- Next action: "Try summarizing major cross-team tickets in the ticket description for the next two sprints; I will review on sprint demos."

Privacy and sensitive issues:
- Never post sensitive HR topics (performance improvement plans, discipline) in a public or semi-public repo.
- For disciplinary or PIP-related feedback, use private feedback entries and escalate to People Ops per the disciplinary playbook.

Quality rubrics (for People Ops and managers to evaluate entry quality):
- Specificity (1–5): Includes concrete examples and links.
- Actionability (1–5): Suggests a clear next step or owner.
- Timeliness (1–5): Feedback was created within an appropriate window after the event.
- Respectfulness (1–5): Tone is professional.

Operational SLOs / targets:
- Adoption: >= 70% of teams using weekly manager synthesis within 6 months of rollout.
- Coverage: No direct report without manager-sourced feedback for >30 days (target 95% compliance).
- Quality: Mean rubric score >= 3.5 after quarter 1 of rollout.

Measurement and reporting cadence:
- People Ops collects weekly adoption metrics and monthly sampled quality reviews (10% of entries).
- Quarterly calibration sessions to review rubric scoring, surface systemic coaching needs, and update templates.

Rollout plan and milestones (recommended 8-week plan):
Week 0: Pilot with two cross-functional pods (Eng infra and SRE).
Week 2: Collect pilot feedback and adjust templates.
Week 4: Expand to product and growth teams.
Week 8: Company-wide launch; People Ops runs manager training and office hours.

Manager training and playbooks:
- 60-minute training: expectations, live demo of creating syntheses, and role-play exercises.
- Office hours weekly for the first 12 weeks.
- Manager checklist (first month): set expectations in 1:1, schedule weekly synthesis, confirm buddy notes, review quality rubric.

Escalation and remediation:
- If manager detects safety issues or persistent performance concerns, follow the existing escalation-playbook (link in related pages) and notify People Ops.
- People Ops will run a 7-day triage review for flagged entries and propose coaching or formal HR steps.

FAQ (short):
Q: Does async feedback replace 1:1s?
A: No. It reduces frequency of synchronous-only items and ensures written record. Use both.
Q: Can anyone read my feedback entries?
A: Only people with repo permissions. Public praise should be posted publicly; coaching stays private.
Q: How do we avoid feedback overload?
A: Use templates; limit task-feedback to 200 words and reserve developmental snapshots for recurring patterns. Managers synthesize to reduce noise.
